classification_signals: The study aims to investigate the architectural cases of biomimicry that currently exist and find structures that appeal to consumers' preferences (Abstract, p. 2).
similar characteristics of consumer-preferred design cases mimicking natural visual elements are confirmed through case analysis (Abstract, p. 2).
This study is performed based on a previous article, namely '10 Stunning Examples of Biomimicry in Architecture' (p. 3).
a comparative analysis was performed on the cases (p. 3).
Tables 5-10 provide 'Comparison of Visual Factors in Morphological Biomimicry Architecture and Prototypes' (pp. 10-11).
title: Analysis of Constituent Elements for Inducing Aesthetic Preferences in Biomimicry Architecture Form Design -Focusing on Arousal Potential in Visual Cognition-

limitations: This study does not assess multiple impacts but analyzes from the visual and cognitive levels.
It is imperative to carry out additional investigations utilizing pertinent variables comprehensively and multifacetedly.
minimum_safe_summary: This case study analyzes biomimicry architectural designs to identify elements that induce aesthetic preferences, focusing on arousal potential in visual cognition. Key findings indicate that consumer-preferred designs balance novelty and familiarity, often by imitating 3-4 out of six visual factors from natural prototypes, particularly structural order. Too much novelty or familiarity can prevent aesthetic preferences, while a moderate arousal potential, achieved through a suitable balance, stimulates positive feelings and dopamine release. The study acknowledges limitations in its scope, focusing primarily on visual and cognitive levels without a comprehensive assessment of multiple impacts.
